headline: YouTube showed new AI tools for creators at its Made on YouTube event, including draft feedback, thumbnail and title suggestions, chat-based editing and wider protection against deepfakes.
score_reason: Real product news, but the event looks to have been held before 6 Oct (RedShark says late September), and the only same-day text found is a one-line Reuters item; score lowered by 1.
importance_line: Creators get AI help with drafting, titles and editing and wider tools to find faces faked by AI, though YouTube has not shown that the tools improve results.
summary: RedShark News reports that at its annual Made on YouTube event YouTube added AI to drafting, thumbnails, testing and editing, including a draft feedback tool, matching title and thumbnail options, A/B tests of video openings and chat-based editing in Shorts and YouTube Create. Likeness detection, which helps people find videos where their face appears AI-altered, is now open to all adults aged 18 and over and is coming to mobile, with speaking-voice detection due later this year; Reuters, as relayed by Interaksyon, also reported the event.
notes: Interaksyon (Reuters text, one sentence only) says "on Wednesday" and is dated 7 Oct 2026; RedShark says the event was held in late September. Dates conflict; exact event day not found, so freshness is flagged as late Sep 2026 and the score lowered by 1 (6 to 5). The summary is built from RedShark.
